subject: religious-studies
title: The Problem of Evil and Theodicy
welcome_lead: If God is all-powerful and all-good, why does evil exist? Walk through theodicies from Augustine to Plantinga.
meta_desc: Religious Studies Adventure: the problem of evil, Augustinian and Irenaean theodicies, free-will defence.
final_note: You have weighed theodicies. The problem of evil remains philosophy of religion's central challenge.

concepts.def: Apparent contradiction between God's omnipotence, omnibenevolence and the existence of evil.
Claim that God's existence is logically incompatible with any evil.
Claim that the amount and distribution of evil makes God's existence unlikely.
Theodicy tracing evil to the misuse of free will by angels and humans (privatio boni).
Theodicy presenting evil as a means of moral and spiritual growth, developed by John Hick (soul-making).
Alvin Plantinga's argument that significant moral freedom necessarily allows the possibility of evil.

walkthroughs.body_html: The classical formulation asks whether God is willing but unable to prevent evil (not omnipotent), able but unwilling (not good), or both — in which case why call it God? J. L. Mackie pressed the logical problem; William Rowe focused on the evidential force of horrendous suffering.

Augustine treated evil as privatio boni — a privation rather than substance. Evil entered creation through the misuse of free will by angels and humans; the Fall transmits original sin. Critics question the goodness of a creation that includes such risk and the coherence of inherited guilt.

John Hick's revival of Irenaean theodicy presents life as a 'vale of soul-making' in which suffering enables moral growth. Plantinga's free-will defence aims at the logical problem: God could not actualise a world of significantly free creatures while guaranteeing they never chose evil.

mcqs.q: What does the teleological (design) argument claim?
options: The design argument proves evolution is false.
Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.
Apparent purpose, order or complexity in the universe implies an intelligent designer — Paley's watchmaker analogy is the classic example.
The design argument proves God created the world in seven days.

mcqs.q: What is the central principle of situation ethics?
options: You should do whatever feels right in the moment.
The cosmological argument proves the Big Bang happened.
The only intrinsically good thing is agape love; rules can be broken if doing so produces the most loving outcome in the situation.
Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.

mcqs.q: What does the cosmological argument try to prove?
options: Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.
The cosmological argument proves the Big Bang happened.
The cosmological argument proves who created life on Earth.
That the existence of the universe requires a first cause or necessary being — usually identified with God — to explain why anything exists at all.
